headline: Advances in Quantum Information, Error Control, and Hardware
summary: Today's research explores foundational quantum information bounds, novel classical post-processing methods for fault tolerance, and experimental control of optical tweezers. Together, these papers push the boundaries of quantum capacity limits, error mitigation, and hardware scalability.

themes.title: Quantum Information Theory and Entanglement
themes.body: New mathematical insights resolve open problems in entanglement distillation and capacity limits. Researchers disproved the equality between the regularised Rains bound and PPT distillable entanglement, and derived exact two-way capacities for pure-loss channels.

themes.title: Quantum Error Correction and Circuit Optimization
themes.body: Novel techniques improve fault tolerance and circuit scaling. Virtual error cancellation drastically reduces logical errors purely through post-processing, while graphical methods efficiently bound entanglement and magic in ZX-diagrams.

themes.title: Quantum Hardware and Machine Learning
themes.body: Experimental control and algorithmic scaling are put to the test. Spatial light modulators achieve site-resolved polarization control in strontium tweezer arrays, while adaptively grown quantum classifiers reveal weak correlation with data-scaling laws on MNIST.

connections.body: Both papers address fundamental limits and properties of quantum entanglement, utilizing advanced operator forms and graphical formalisms like ZX-calculus to bound non-classical resources.
